metadata.description: Personal Claude Code plugin marketplace by Charalampos Kyfonidis

plugins.name: agent-step-toolkit
plugins.description: Build agent-step LangGraph agents — a ReAct agent fronted by one batching tool over a deterministic flow-controller runner (vendored and versioned; agent-step 3.0.1). Bootstrap a project (runner library + streaming CLI + graph/state/prompt scaffold + the required local sandbox service), then add domain tools declaratively: each action declares its params, prereqs and verdict ROWS — summary, doctrine, state write, effects, one authority per outcome — and its executor just names the verdict. The engine owns the machinery and the model-facing language it enforces: composed action descriptions, per-gate reply contracts, the spliceable turn-protocol prompt fragment, and engine-rendered read-backs and standing asks the model speaks verbatim. Mechanisms are configuration, not prompt prose — confirmation propose/execute gates with attempt budgets and stored-byte repetition, OTP and double-entry match gates, multi-turn flows, paginated reads, escalation ladders that count the prompt's "once" rules and escalate themselves, capture-bounce bounds, an engine-enforced abort policy, typed handoff routes, and a state-resolved handback envelope with orchestrator/specialized agent roles plus off-topic delegation. Graph state is one Zod schema (reducers + invoke-boundary validation, channel-completeness enforced at construction). Also: flow documentation for any agent-step agent (from a prose description, an existing codebase, or specs and a walkthrough — one validated spec generating a Markdown design, an auto-laid-out interactive step graph and an xlsx step sheet, with a verification script), caller-capture param primitives, the twelve measured host-architecture design principles, porting an existing project onto agent-step, Kafka run-tracing observability via the companion kafka-observability plugin, the three-layer test methodology (runner unit / sandbox / prompt-input), and a channel-middleware contract audit.

plugins.name: langgraph-plugin
plugins.description: Run and debug LangGraph.js conversations: /run-langgraph-conversation executes a single- or multi-turn test conversation against the local dev server — finding the running instance that serves the project on any port before starting one — and captures the thread, with an opt-in raw SSE streaming capture (token/handoff/custom event order); /follow-langgraph-conversation investigates any thread end-to-end: locates the instance that OWNS the thread, inventories the available monitoring sources (dev-server checkpoint history, LangSmith traces incl. EU/self-hosted endpoints, process/container logs), reads handoff signals and step-batch tool envelopes, and produces root-cause analysis. Discovers ports, owning instances, graph ids, and LangSmith credentials/endpoint from the project's own config and the live environment (langgraph.json, dev script, docker-compose, .env, running processes/containers).

plugins.name: kafka-observability
plugins.description: LangSmith-parity observability over Kafka for any LangGraph.js / LangChain.js agent: /add-kafka-observability installs or upgrades a vendored src/observability/ library that attaches a BaseTracer subclass globally through two redundant paths — the configure hook plus the configure-slot LangSmith's own tracer occupies, so it attaches even on platform runtimes that sever async-context ancestry (one startup() call, zero per-node instrumentation) — and publishes EVERY traced run — graph invocation, LangGraph nodes, LLM calls with full prompts/outputs/token usage, tool runs, errors, trace hierarchy, plus opt-in backend HTTP call runs via the traceBackendCall helper — as start/end events to a Kafka topic (standard envelope keyed by event id, thread_id correlation, zod-validated, secret-redacted, 512KB-truncated) over a bounded non-blocking fire-and-forget producer (librdkafka, acks=all, idempotent, bounded shutdown). By default EVERY run is emitted (full LangSmith parity); apps that have payload-verified which of their runs duplicate root/llm/tool content can opt into run filtering (KAFKA_RUN_FILTER_MODE=allow|deny + run_type:name globs, the name side also matching metadata.langgraph_node; the root run always survives — it carries the full invocation input/final state and is the turn-boundary marker for timeline consumers). Disabled by default (KAFKA_ENABLED); runs alongside LangSmith for parallel validation so LangSmith can be unplugged with no code change. Conversation content (prompts, completions, graph state, tool params) is masked by a policy the APPLICATION supplies — startup({ contentMask }) plus digit/deep-walk primitives that compose with a domain masker the project already owns, covering both numeral runs and digits SPOKEN as words (Greek + English packs, inflection/accent-tolerant — how PINs and OTPs actually arrive on a voice channel); the library ships the SEAM, not the policy (which digits are a tax id and which an order reference is a fact about the app's flow, not about Kafka), applies it at the single emit funnel to inputs/outputs/error/events[].kwargs, leaves trace identity, the timeline, metadata and JSON numbers untouched, and masks nothing until one is wired. Startup logs one-line attachment diagnostics (core copy, ALS state, injected loader flags) and warns loudly when the runtime forces the fallback path. Intake proposes broker/topic/security defaults discovered from sibling repos in the workspace that already carry the library (propose-only; the user confirms every value). The skill also wires the client dependency, .env.example, deployment settings with Key Vault refs, a test script, and verifies with typecheck + the library's unit suite. Detects pre-existing Kafka functionality first (foreign src/observability/ modules, producers elsewhere) and asks the user to classify it — agent-flow observability (keep-both or replace with downstream sign-off) vs unrelated e.g. liveness/business events (always preserved) — never overwriting a foreign module.
